chose: A spoken cards essay is the same cut list (some-ui.cut-list/2) with one optional field on a shot, `spoken`: the intro (`said`), a scene (`chapter` and `narration`) or the close (`said`). The cheat-sheet series' version 2, which adds the captions design, is what makes an essay spoken: in it every scene must say something, the first is the intro and only the last may be the close. Version 1 stays silent and refuses `spoken`. The intro and close are scenes with a card picture of their own, so they show something while they are said. `durationMs` is still written but the take sets each scene's length. A scene's chapter line and its narration are two takes, the host's and the narrator's, joined into the scene's one take with half a second between, so the card is drawn once under both. Each chapter line, without its "Chapter one." lead, titles a chapter in the upload's description, and the close is titled "What to do next".
options: an optional `spoken` field on a shot, gated by cheat-sheet v2, its two lines joined into one take
a new cut-list schema, some-ui.cut-list/3, with a separate list of lines
the chapter line as its own scene over the same card, which draws the card twice

Whether the intro and close are scenes, whether durationMs stays written, and whether a chapter line is heard as its own beat are the owner's to notice when writing or watching an essay.
undo: Have cardsScenes give a scene one line, its chapter and narration in one voice; to drop the shape, pin cheat-sheet v3 without the captions design and drop the `spoken` checks from parseCardsEssay. The field is optional, so no essay breaks.
